attempts: {"key_idea":"A recursive function stops when some input is handled directly, without making another recursive call.","body":"Take a countdown function: countdown(n) prints n and calls countdown(n-1). Written that way, it would run forever, going 3, 2, 1, 0, -1, and so on. If we add the line 'if n == 3 ... stop', the chain ends the moment n reaches that value, because that case never calls countdown again.","question":"Looking at your own factorial function, which line handles an input directly without calling factorial again, and what does it return for 0?"}

output.body: Take countdown(n), which prints n and then calls countdown(n-1). Alone, it would run forever: 3, 2, 1, 0, -1, and on. Adding the line 'if n == 0, return' ends the chain, because that case never calls countdown again.
output.key_idea: A recursive function stops when some input is handled directly, without making another recursive call.
